key_insight: Combining data augmentation with experience replay (memory manipulation) around a Mamba-based language model enables sample-efficient generation of property-optimized small molecules — achieving strong optimization with far fewer training examples/evaluations.
problem_solved: Generative molecular design often requires large datasets and many costly property evaluations; this work tackles low sample efficiency by reusing and augmenting useful examples so models learn to produce high-quality, property-optimized molecules faster.
method: Train a Mamba-based molecular language model to generate SMILES/graph representations of small molecules.
Apply targeted data augmentation to expand training signals from limited high-quality examples.
Use experience replay / memory manipulation: maintain a buffer of promising molecules and periodically replay them during training to bias generation toward desirable properties.
impact: Makes property-driven molecular generation more practical by reducing data and compute needs, accelerating iterative design cycles in drug discovery and materials. Practitioners can integrate augmentation + replay to boost optimization returns from existing models without massive new datasets.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: Mamba LM → data augmentation → memory buffer (experience replay) → optimized molecule outputs

paper_title: Sample-efficient generative molecular design using memory manipulation
paper_authors: Jeff Guo, Junwu Chen, Anthony GX-Chen, Philippe Schwaller
